_about.what: The reference variety of each family: the one every other variety in its equivalence class is contrasted against. Turns an N×N dialect problem into N−1 pairs — Arabic's 26 regional tags are 325 pairs and 25 contrasts — and it is what makes two results in one family comparable, because they were measured against the same baseline.
_about.not-a-ranking: It is the contrast baseline, not the correct, best or standard variety. Nothing here is a claim about prestige or priority; it is a statement about what a measurement is relative to. The file is read by people whose own variety is on the other side of it.
_about.complete-on-purpose: EVERY contrastable family in the shipped locale list has an entry, including the ones a rule could derive (pt/PT, ru/RU, es/ES). Deriving them meant the file showed only exceptions, so the families nobody had thought about were invisible — and the first member of the class quietly stood in for a decision. One file, one entry per family, is what makes the open questions countable and the settled ones arguable.
_about.keyed-by: Equivalence class `iso639-3|script`. A reference is a statement about regions *within* one writing system — Serbian needs one per alphabet, and a contrast that crossed that line would measure the script rather than the variety.
_about.the-baseline: `baseline` is the tag every other variety in the family is contrasted against, written in the conventional BCP-47 form — `en-US`, `sr-Cyrl-RS` — whatever the loaded locale list happens to spell it. It is resolved by what the tag means — primary subtag, region, script — rather than by how it is spelled, so one file serves a list that writes `sr-Latn-RS` and one that writes `sr-rs-latn`. A baseline naming a variety the loaded list does not carry is reported by `polyglot references --check` and never silently substituted.
_about.not-per-scheme: One file for every locale list. Which variety baselines a family does not change when you load a different list; only the spelling of the tag does, which is what the lenient resolution above is for. A family this file does not cover still runs: `core/reference.py` falls back to the subtag rule and then to the first member, both labelled as what they are.
four-states: `reviewed: true`   — recorded. A person stood behind this baseline; it is what a scan uses.

`reviewed: false`  — proposed. Written down with a reason, nobody has confirmed it. A scan leaves these out unless asked for them explicitly, because a verdict measured against an unconfirmed baseline is a claim nobody made.
`baseline: null`   — decided that this family has no defensible baseline. A finished decision, not a gap.
absent            — a family this file does not cover. Should not happen for the shipped list; `polyglot references --check` is what says so.
_about.how-to-confirm: Read the `why`, change the `region` if it is wrong, and set `reviewed` to true. That is the whole workflow, and it is deliberately a file rather than a screen: a baseline is an argument, and an argument belongs in review with a diff.
_about.human-readable-half: `language`, `script` and `baseline_title` are a reading aid, not data: the resolver uses `baseline`, `why` and `reviewed` and nothing else. `polyglot references --annotate` refreshes them from the loaded list, and `--check` reports any that have gone stale.

aar|Latn.why: Most Afar speakers live in Ethiopia's Afar Region, where the Latin orthography is taught; Djibouti and Eritrea are the contrast arms. Alphabetical order had put Djibouti here.

afr|Latn.why: Afrikaans is codified in South Africa; Namibian Afrikaans is the contrast arm. Alphabetical order had put Namibia here.

aka|Latn.why: Two language subtags share Ghana (`ak`, `tw`), so a region cannot name one row. Akan proper baselines the class and Twi is the contrast arm — which is the arguable half of this entry, since Twi is the larger written variety.

ara|Arab.why: Operator decision. The alternative baseline is Modern Standard Arabic, which is not a region and so cannot be a member of this class; SA is the closest regional standard to it.

aym|Latn.why: `ay` and `ayr` both carry BO. Bolivia holds most Aymara speakers and the orthography in official use; the macrolanguage row baselines the class rather than Central Aymara (`ayr`).

aze|Latn.why: North Azerbaijani as written in Azerbaijan. Named as a tag rather than a region because the class also files `az-AZ-Cyrl`, and a Cyrillic baseline would make every contrast in it measure the alphabet.

ben|Beng.why: Standard literary Bengali is shared across the border, so this is a population call rather than a linguistic one: Bangladesh has roughly twice West Bengal's speakers. `bn-IN` is the defensible alternative and the reason this is not marked reviewed.

bod|Tibt.why: Lhasa Tibetan is the written standard; the exile variety in India is the contrast arm.

cat|Latn.why: The rule cannot fire — Catalan is `ca` and Spain is `ES`, and `CA` is Canada. Without an entry the first member stood in, which is `ca-AD`: Andorran Catalan is Central Catalan with a different passport, so contrasting `ca-ES` against it would measure nothing, and Roussillonnais (FR) and Alguèrs (IT) would be held against the smallest Catalan-speaking polity rather than the one the written standard is codified in.

dan|Latn.why: The rule cannot fire: Danish is `da` and Denmark is `DK`. Greenlandic Danish is the contrast arm.

deu|Latn.why: The language subtag equals the region subtag (de/DE), which is this project's uniform rule for a baseline. Written down rather than derived, so the family is visible here beside the ones that needed an argument.

ell|Grek.why: The rule cannot fire: Greek is `el` and Greece is `GR`. Cypriot Greek is the contrast arm.

eng|Latn.why: The rule cannot fire — there is no `en-EN`. US over GB: it is what CLDR likelySubtags resolves bare `en` to, and `markers/english.json` already expresses every sibling against the American forms, so a different choice here would contradict the marker sets.

ewe|Latn.why: The standard Ewe orthography is the Ghanaian one and the Volta Region holds most speakers; Togo is the contrast arm.

fas|Arab.why: The rule cannot fire: Persian is `fa` and Iran is `IR`. Dari (`fa-AF`) is the contrast arm.

fra|Latn.why: The language subtag equals the region subtag (fr/FR), which is this project's uniform rule for a baseline. Written down rather than derived, so the family is visible here beside the ones that needed an argument.

gla|Latn.why: Scottish Gaelic is codified in Scotland. Alphabetical order had put Canadian Gaelic — a few thousand speakers in Nova Scotia — here.

gsw|Latn.why: Swiss German is the bulk of this class; Alsatian (FR) and Liechtenstein are the contrast arms. The list's own name for the class is Alsatian, which is worth settling before this is confirmed.

hau|Latn.why: Kano Hausa is the written standard and Nigeria holds most speakers; Niger and Ghana are the contrast arms. Alphabetical order had put Ghana here.

ita|Latn.why: The language subtag equals the region subtag (it/IT), which is this project's uniform rule for a baseline. Written down rather than derived, so the family is visible here beside the ones that needed an argument.

kon|Latn.why: `kg` and `kon` both carry AO, so a region cannot name one row. Which of the two the list means by each is unclear, and this entry should not be confirmed until that is.

kur|Arab.why: In Arabic script the written standard is Sorani as used in Iraqi Kurdistan; Iran is the contrast arm. Kurmanji is written in Latin and is a different class.

lav|Latn.why: `lav` and `lvs` both carry LV, so a region cannot name one row. The macrolanguage row baselines the class; Standard Latvian (`lvs`) is the same variety under a narrower code, which makes this pair a poor contrast and worth questioning as a family at all.

lin|Latn.why: Kinshasa Lingala is the variety with institutional weight and the largest speaker base; Congo-Brazzaville, Angola and CAR are the contrast arms. Alphabetical order had put Angola here.

lrc|Arab.why: Northern Luri is spoken overwhelmingly in Iran; the Iraqi row is the contrast arm. Alphabetical order had put Iraq here.

mas|Latn.why: Maasai spans the Kenya–Tanzania border with no codified standard on either side; Kenya is proposed on speaker numbers alone.

mon|Cyrl.why: The subtag rule fires (mn/MN), but `khk-mn` shares the region, so the region alone cannot name the row. Khalkha is the standard either way; the macrolanguage row baselines the class.

msa|Latn.why: `ms` and `zsm` both carry MY, so a region cannot name one row. Malaysia's Bahasa Melayu baselines the class; Brunei and Singapore are the contrast arms. Alphabetical order had put Brunei here.

nep|Deva.why: Nepali is codified in Nepal; the Indian row (Sikkim, Darjeeling) is the contrast arm. Alphabetical order had put India here.

nld|Latn.why: The language subtag equals the region subtag (nl/NL), which is this project's uniform rule for a baseline. Written down rather than derived, so the family is visible here beside the ones that needed an argument.

orm|Latn.why: `gaz` and `om` both carry ET, so a region cannot name one row. Ethiopia holds the Oromo standard and the Qubee orthography; Kenya is the contrast arm. Whether the macrolanguage row or West Central Oromo (`gaz`) should baseline it is the open half.

oss|Cyrl.why: North Ossetia holds the Iron standard and most speakers; South Ossetia/Georgia is the contrast arm.

por|Latn.why: The language subtag equals the region subtag (pt/PT), which is this project's uniform rule for a baseline. Written down rather than derived, so the family is visible here beside the ones that needed an argument.

pus|Arab.why: Pashto is an official language of Afghanistan and standardised there; the Pakistani row is the contrast arm.

que|Latn.why: PROPOSED UNDER PROTEST: the list files Cusco Quechua (`quz`) under Bolivia and Ecuador and carries no Peruvian row, which looks like a defect in the locale list — Cusco is in Peru. Bolivia stands in so the family is not left headless; this should be resolved in the list rather than confirmed here.

ron|Latn.why: The language subtag equals the region subtag (ro/RO), which is this project's uniform rule for a baseline. Written down rather than derived, so the family is visible here beside the ones that needed an argument.

rus|Cyrl.why: The language subtag equals the region subtag (ru/RU), which is this project's uniform rule for a baseline. Written down rather than derived, so the family is visible here beside the ones that needed an argument.

sma|Latn.why: Southern Sami straddles Norway and Sweden with orthographies on both sides. Norway is proposed on speaker numbers; this is close enough to be worth a second opinion.

sme|Latn.why: Northern Sami: the subtag rule fires (se/SE). Norway holds more speakers, so this is the one rule-derived baseline worth re-reading — left as the rule has it until somebody who works in the family says otherwise.

smj|Latn.why: Lule Sami is centred on Jokkmokk in Sweden, where the orthography was codified; Norway is the contrast arm. Alphabetical order had put Norway here.

som|Latn.why: The language subtag equals the region subtag (so/SO), which is this project's uniform rule for a baseline. Written down rather than derived, so the family is visible here beside the ones that needed an argument.

sot|Latn.why: Sesotho is codified in Lesotho, where it is the sole national language; South African Sesotho is the contrast arm and uses a different orthography, which is exactly what makes this pair worth measuring.

spa|Latn.why: The language subtag equals the region subtag (es/ES), which is this project's uniform rule for a baseline. Written down rather than derived, so the family is visible here beside the ones that needed an argument.

sqi|Latn.why: Standard Albanian is codified in Albania on the Tosk base; North Macedonia and Kosovo are the contrast arms.

srp|Cyrl.why: The rule cannot fire: Serbian is `sr` and Serbia is `RS`. Serbia baselines both Serbian classes; Montenegro, Bosnia and Kosovo are the varieties contrasted against it.

srp|Latn.why: As `srp|Cyrl`, in the other alphabet. A reference never crosses a script class.

ssw|Latn.why: siSwati is the national language of Eswatini; the South African row is the contrast arm.

swa|Latn.why: Standard Swahili is codified on the Kiunguja (Zanzibar) base and Tanzania is where it is an official national language; Kenya, Uganda and DR Congo are the contrast arms. Alphabetical order had put DR Congo here.

swe|Latn.why: The rule cannot fire: Swedish is `sv` and Sweden is `SE`. Finland and Åland Swedish are the varieties under contrast.

tam|Taml.why: Tamil Nadu holds the written standard; Sri Lanka, Singapore and Malaysia are the contrast arms — Sri Lankan Tamil being the one with real lexical distance from it.

teo|Latn.why: Most Iteso live in Uganda; the Kenyan row is the contrast arm. Alphabetical order had put Kenya here.

tir|Ethi.why: Tigrinya is an official language of Eritrea and the Asmara press standardised much of the written form, but Tigray holds more speakers — a genuine split, and the reason this is proposed rather than confirmed.

tur|Latn.why: The language subtag equals the region subtag (tr/TR), which is this project's uniform rule for a baseline. Written down rather than derived, so the family is visible here beside the ones that needed an argument.

tzm|Latn.why: Standard Moroccan Tamazight is the codified variety in Latin script; the Algerian row is the contrast arm. Alphabetical order had put Algeria here.

urd|Arab.why: Urdu is the national language of Pakistan and standardised there; the Indian row is the contrast arm. Alphabetical order had put India here.

yor|Latn.why: Standard Yoruba is codified in Nigeria, which holds the overwhelming majority of speakers; Benin is the contrast arm. Alphabetical order had put Benin here.

zho|Hans.why: Simplified Chinese. The class also holds a regionless `zh-hans`, which is a script label rather than a variety anything can be contrasted against.

zho|Hant.why: Traditional Chinese. TW over HK: Hong Kong written Chinese carries Cantonese lexis, a second dimension of difference that would make every contrast against it measure two things at once.
